faq.question: Which agents can use REA?
faq.answer: Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the supported agents; other clients can use manual MCP registration.

faq.question: Do I need Hopper, Ghidra or IDA?
faq.answer: Deep native analysis uses one of them. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra and IDA use your existing installations. See provider setup.

faq.question: Do I need to start Hopper first?
faq.answer: REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open Hopper manually if needed. See Hopper startup and troubleshooting.

faq.question: What does installing the skill from skills.sh do?
faq.answer: The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use npx rea-agents setup to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See skill-only installation.

faq.question: What code does REA return?
faq.answer: Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the showcases give worked examples.

faq.question: Does REA upload my app?
faq.answer: REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy.

faq.question: What should I do if I hit a bug?
faq.answer: Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For a CLI installed with npm install --global or bun add --global: ``bash rea update ` For agent setup through npx: `bash npx rea-agents@latest setup `` If you're using an agent, complete the setup refresh and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, open an issue with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.
